summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update2.json → valid=true). Independent second A2 direction, source-only since this run's experiment capacity is exhausted. Trace: the explicit-target transfer API checks only 'not to itself' (raft.go:2187-2206) while the automatic path filters to voters via pickServer (raft.go:2166-2169), and startStopReplication creates replication state for every configured peer except the local one (raft.go:583-611) — so the catch-up loop in leadershipTransfer (raft.go:989-1030) terminates for a non-voting target and sends TimeoutNow. The non-voter is then put into candidacy, electSelf persists currentTerm+1 and asks only voters (raft.go:1976-1984), and each voter adopts the newer term and becomes Follower *before* rejecting the vote as non-voter (raft.go:1660-1684, with the ordering documented at 1673-1677) — so the target can never win, yet the incumbent leader is removed. The caller-visible outcome contradicts the captured API contract ('If a follower cannot be promoted, it will fail gracefully', api.go:1259-1260/1274-1275) because the future is resolved with nil on the leftLeaderLoop branch (raft.go:734-739, 748-756), i.e. success is justified by the leader leaving its loop rather than by the target acquiring leadership. Recorded as: one new investigation (@q_transfer_target_suffrage, using the previously saved TimeoutNow behavior as knowledge use), a Behavior (unvalidated explicit target vs. voter-filtered automatic path) and a Fact (non-voter target costs leadership while the future still reports success), plus an 'explained' interpretation with counterevidence and explicit limits (source-established, no receipt; caller-reachable; the follow-up election timing is schedule-dependent and not claimed).
